Cc: platform@novamed.com

Subject: Post-demo notes and next tests

Jordan — thanks again for the demo today. Quick notes from our side and a couple of asks so we can align internally with infra and procurement: 

1) Our main open question is head-to-head behavior under steady-state concurrency: 2k RPS sustained for 12 hours with p95 latency <= 120ms. We need to see realistic tail behavior, not just single-shot latency numbers.
2) We want to validate cold-start / scale-up behavior during a traffic surge (10x for 10 minutes).
3) Cost sensitivity: compute amortized cost per 1M tokens and expected token throughput per reserved GPU hour.
4) Security/compliance: can you confirm that logs/KV cache never leave our VPC during Private deployment? (Ops needs explicit wording for our SOC2 review)

Can you propose concrete tests we can run next week? Also please send any benchmark templates you prefer — I tossed an outline (attached).

Cheers,
Bryan
Director, Platform Engineering
NovaMed

Bryan — great to hear this captured your team’s priorities. Below is a concrete, prioritized test plan and what we’ll deliver for each bullet. I copied Grace and Markus for ops and pricing specifics.

Summary of proposed tests (short-run, reproducible):

A) Steady-state concurrency run (lab):
- Target: 2k RPS sustained for 12 hours against your representative prompt set (you provided sample prompts).
- Measurements: p50/p95/p99 latency, token/sec, GPU utilization, memory pressure, and token cost.
- Environment: Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) vs Hyperscaler reserved instances (your cloud account VM sizes). We will use identical model bits (quantization profile) where possible; if not, we’ll map to closest variant and annotate differences.
- Deliverable: time-series CSV + latency histograms, configuration files, and a short readme.

B) Surge / scale-up:
- Target: 10x burst for 10 minutes from 200 RPS -> 2k RPS; measure scale-up time, transient p99s, and any dropped/queued requests.
- Deliverable: step-load logs and explanation of autoscaling/fallback behavior.

C) Amortized cost analysis:
- We’ll produce per-1M-token cost estimates under the test profiles above for: Redwood Dedicated (reserved), Redwood Hosted fallback, and the Hyperscaler reserved instance path. We’ll include assumptions (batch sizes, KV cache hit rates).

D) Security confirmation:
- For Private deployments we provide: architecture blurb (single-tenant control plane), KV cache lifecycle, and KMS integration notes. Markus will draft the SOC2-friendly statement.

Next steps / timeline:
- We can run a lab pass on Wed 6/2 and deliver preliminary graphs by EOD Thu 6/3. Full artifacts by Mon 6/7.
- If that works, Markus: can you confirm the pricing extract (reserved vs burst) and attach the bench template? Grace: can you lead the run and tell us which infra knobs we should set on NovaMed’s side?

Happy to sync on a 30-minute call if you want to walk through the test plan.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Bryan — quick ops notes on the run itself so we’re aligned on inputs: 

- Prompts: please confirm the canonical set (at least 250 unique requests) and indicate which requests expect multi-turn state (to include KV cache considerations).
- Traffic generator: we prefer k6 with the shared scenario in the attached sheet (replay + synthetic ramp).
- Metrics hooks: enable request_id in headers; expose: latency_ms, tokens_generated, gpu_util_pct, kv_hit (bool). If you can add cloudwatch/GCP metrics endpoints we can cross-validate.
- Hyperscaler mapping: send the VM SKU list you plan to test; we’ll map to GPU type and recommended instance counts. Small note: hyperscaler CPU-bound requests during quantized runs can look cheaper but will show far worse p99s under 2k RPS sustained.

I’ll own the run orchestration and collection; Jordan and Markus will handle model mapping and cost calc.

—Grace
Director, Solutions & Performance
Redwood Inference
